 Avon investment adviser pleads guilty in $3.3M fraud scheme
 A gavel. Contributed Photo | PIXABAY 
 By Greg Bordonaro 
 October 23, 2026 
 Share 
 Copy URL Email Facebook X Linkedin 
 Andrew Komarow used $8.9 million in unfunded transfers to make risky options trades, leaving three financial firms with major losses, prosecutors said.

 An Avon investment adviser has pleaded guilty to wire fraud after using unfunded bank transfers to finance speculative trades, leaving three financial services companies with combined losses of about $3.3 million, federal prosecutors said.
Andrew M. Komarow, 37, entered the plea before U.S. District Judge Vernon D. Oliver in Hartford.
Between approximately October 2022 and February 2023, Komarow initiated about $8.9 million in electronic transfers from personal bank accounts to brokerage accounts, despite lacking enough money to complete the transfers, prosecutors said.
He exploited the time needed to process those transactions, using credit provided by the financial services companies to make high-risk, short-term options trades. His goal was to generate quick profits that would cover the unfunded transfers, according to prosecutors.
The companies lost a total of $3,352,507.
Komarow faces up to 20 years in prison. A sentencing date has not been set. He was arrested March 2, 2026, and remains free on a $50,000 bond.
